title: docs(qa): revise cli.doctor-health-report to revision 2 — the monorepo-anchored expected-fail is now a pass
body:
Fixes #10798

Revises `cli.doctor-health-report` in `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/cli.json` to **revision 2**. One item, one revision, one `history` entry — no other item in that file is touched (it is the hot shared file of the #10663 QA-run lane).

## Why now

The item's last acceptance clause was an EXPECTED-FAIL recording a live product defect: `findMissingTests` / `findDeprecatedUsages` walked only `<cwd>/packages/spec/src` and printed `✓ Test coverage` / `✓ Deprecations` about a tree they never opened. #10679 landed the fix, so the clause had to invert or the item would instruct a runner to record a failure that no longer happens.

## Written against a real run, not against the source

The clause a runner executes is an instruction, so the text was written from observed output. The shipped CLI was built from this base and driven in a real `create-objectstack -t blank` scaffold, and again from a monorepo checkout for the counterpart. Scaffold, verbatim:

```
  ℹ Test coverage         Skipped — no packages/spec/src in this directory (monorepo-only check)
  ℹ Deprecations          Skipped — no packages/spec/src in this directory (monorepo-only check)
```

and under `-v`, beneath each:

```
      → Looked for <cwd>/packages/spec/src and found nothing to walk. This check reads the
        monorepo's own spec sources, so outside that checkout it has no subject — and a ✓ here
        would be a claim about files doctor never opened.
```

Neither old `✓` appears, neither `→ Checking…` step line appears, and the `@objectstack/spec  Not built` row is absent — its probe is now gated on `<cwd>/packages/spec/package.json`. From the monorepo the scanned arm still runs: `✓ @objectstack/spec    Built`, the step lines, and the real `⚠` findings all print.

## The measurement corrected more than the card predicted

The card expected one row in the first acceptance clause's enumeration to have become conditional (`@objectstack/spec`). The real report shows the enumeration was wrong about a second row too, and had been since revision 1: **`Installed packages` was never unconditional** — `installedPackageLedgerChecks` returns `[]` on a clean ledger, so the row appears only on a ledger failure or a skipped entry. That also contradicted the item's own clause 4, which describes it as a *failure* row. `NODE_ENV` and `Tenancy posture` are finding-only for the same reason.

So the clause now splits **unconditional** rows (Node.js, pnpm, TypeScript, Dependencies, Git, Environment files) from **finding-only** rows, each with the condition that produces it, rather than naming a single exception.

## What changed in the item

- **title** — the tail declared the two `✓`s an expected-fail; rewritten to the skip behaviour.
- **acceptance[0]** — row enumeration split unconditional vs finding-only; `verify` re-anchored.
- **acceptance[7]** — EXPECTED-FAIL inverted into an ordinary pass clause, with the `printInfo`-not-`printWarning` invariant stated (withholding a false `✓` must not manufacture a false `⚠`).
- **steps[0]** and **steps[6]** — the enumeration, and the old "capture the two `✓` lines" step, rewritten to capture the skip rows and assert three absences.
- **negative** — the `@objectstack/spec  Not built` entry flipped from an accepted note into a regression; two negatives added for the skip row's own wrong shapes (a `⚠` instead of a `ℹ`, and the row vanishing instead of printing).
- **fixtures** — the `requires` note now says both cwds must be run; the `knownGaps` `configExists()` anchor re-derived.
- **source** — `doctor-unexamined-spec-tree.test.ts` added to the unit pins.
- **every line anchor in the item re-derived at this base.** `doctor.ts` grew ~90 lines, so every number quoted at revision 1 had moved — including the ones in clauses this card did not otherwise touch.

## Verification — union run at `0e833d5`

| gate | verdict line |
|---|---|
| `pnpm check:doc-authoring` | `✓ doc authoring guard: 389 files clean — no bare metadata literals.` |
| `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` | `✓ check:doc-formula-expressions: 22 record-scoped formula example(s) across 420 files / 1447 TS blocks judged clean` |
| `pnpm check:nul-bytes` | `check-nul-bytes: OK (scanned 6400 text file(s) … no raw ASCII control bytes).` |
| `pnpm lint` (repo-wide `eslint . --no-inline-config`, not narrowed) | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:platform-checklist` | `1 problem(s)` — **pre-existing**, see below |

Gate families derived from the tree with `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` against the actual change set, not from a recalled list.

`check:platform-checklist` reports exactly one problem, `coverage.json · manifest: UNCLASSIFIED`, and it is **not from this change**: reverting `cli.json` to `bb006446` and re-running produced the identical single problem and the identical exit 1, and the problem names a file this PR does not touch. Filed separately as #11421. Nothing in the run names `cli.json`, so the revision bookkeeping this gate does enforce is well-formed.

## Scope

- No `packages/cli/**` — the code fix already landed.
- No changeset: this publishes nothing. `skip-changeset` applied, matching the precedent for checklist-maintenance PRs (#7636, #7638, #7716, #7717).
- Out of scope, filed rather than folded in: #11420 (the sibling item `cli.doctor-deprecation-scan` is stale on the same two counts — a hint that #10680 already rewrote, and a full anchor set moved by #10679) and #11421.
